newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Strong Irish credit growth sparked rate rise - C.Ban.
newsitem.headline: Strong Irish credit growth sparked rate rise - C.Ban.

text.p: Ireland's Central Bank governor Maurice O'Connell said on Tuesday that although he never attributed interest rate rises to one factor, the bank's surprise half point rate rise on May 1 was influenced by Ireland's strong credit growth figure.

"We never attribute an interest rate adjustment to any precise factor. We make a decision on the basis of the overall situation," O'Connell told a news conference at the launch of the bank's annual report.
"But I will remind you that the credit figures that came out the same day were exceptionally high and we would feel they warranted some response," he said.
O'Connell said the two biggest inflationary risks in Ireland were strong credit growth and rising house prices.
The adjusted annual rate of growth of Irish private sector credit rose to 18.6 percent in March from 15.8 percent in February.
The annual rate of increase in non-mortgage Irish-pound credit rose to 20.7 percent in March from 17.4 percent the previosu month.
Central bank figures also showed that the annual rate of increase in residential mortgate lending was 14.3 percent in March versus 14.0 percent in February.
The bank raised its Short Term Facility lending rate 50 basis points to 6.75 percent effective May 1.
